chunks: Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Aban ibn Taghlib, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Three hundred and thirteen will come to your mosque — that is in Mecca. The people of Mecca will know that their fathers and grandfathers did not give birth to them. They will have swords upon them. Written on each sword is a word that opens to a thousand words. The wind will be sent and call out in every valley: 'This is the Mahdi, who will judge with the judgment of the family of David.' He will not be asked for any proof/evidence regarding him.

key_terms.ثَلَاثَمِائَةٍ وَثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ: Three hundred and thirteen (number of companions)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the Mahdi's arrival in Mecca according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights the eschatological sign of the Mahdi’s arrival in Mecca, where 313 distinct companions will bear swords inscribed with a divine word that expands into a thousand, signaling their unique spiritual authority. The wind’s proclamation in every valley emphasizes the universal recognition of his rule, which is characterized by restoring the justice of the House of David (Adil al-Dawud) without requiring further evidence (bayyinah). This narrative underscores the Shia belief in the Mahdi’s pre-ordained legitimacy and the miraculous nature of his initial emergence.
